# Creating an instance runs nothing

`rimsky instance create` materializes the node graph and does nothing else.
Invoking work is a separate act.

## The template

```yaml
name: audit-idle
version: v1
nodes:
  - type: root
    executor: verifier-shape-checks
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          checks:
            type: array
            default:
              - kind: row_count_absolute
                config:
                  min: 0
```

## Create

```bash
rimsky template register template.yml --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
rimsky template deploy "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
rimsky instance create "$TPL" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
```

The call returns an instance id.

## Nothing has run

```bash
rimsky instance nodes "$IID" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
rimsky instance events "$IID" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages"
```

The `root` node is listed, so the graph exists. Every run counter reads zero —
`active_count`, `pending_count` and `fresh_count`. The event log is empty. The
message queue is empty.

To be sure this is not just a scheduler that has not got there yet: create a
second instance, wake it, and drive it to `work_completed`. Then re-read the
first. It still has no events and still has zero run counters.

Creating an instance has no side effect an operator has to undo or wait out.

## Invoke the work

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"type":""}'
```

The instance runs to `work_completed`. The work was available on demand and was
only ever waiting to be asked for.
